notes.title: Don’t Wake the Best is here! Check out my new project 🐲
notes.content:
Gamers! 

I'm so happy to be writing to you after such a long time! Since Flooded set sail, it’s been an unforgettable journey. And today, I’m thrilled to announce my new game, Don’t Wake the Beast!

This time, I’m diving into a roguelite stealth adventure where treasure hunting meets high-stakes danger. You’ll sneak through randomly generated dungeons, dodge traps and enemies, and - most importantly - steal treasures without waking the Beast. 

Every step counts… And every treasure brings you closer to being caught.

[previewyoutube=oAE7xReD7oo;full][/previewyoutube]

Yep, it’s a different genre, but if you enjoyed Flooded, I’d love for you to check out the trailer for Don’t Wake the Beast and add it to your wishlist. 

Just click the banner below:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3258580/Dont_Wake_the_Beast/

Your support means the world, and I can’t wait to hear what you think of this new adventure. Stay tuned, and thanks for being part of this journey!

See ya,

notes.title: Post-Release Update #4 - New decorations and some bug fixes…
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/f13ad03fe3ea54b6a0cd558db892a201227a5d6d.png

Hello! 

Recently I took some time off to recharge my batteries, and now I'm back with even more energy to bring you a brand new update for Flooded.

Speaking of which… It is now available and packed with some great features! They include three new decorations on different levels (Calm Ocean, Stormy Ocean, and North Ocean) and an entirely new technology - Demolition II.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/99dae4f4d72719d2dc2446f36f5ce10539536063.png

I've also taken care of a bunch of bugs and glitches that were reported some time ago. Now the game will be even more enjoyable.

You'll find the complete changelog below, so make sure to check it out:

New features:
- 1 new technology (Demolition II)
- 1 new decoration on Calm Ocean
- 1 new decoration on Stormy Ocean
- 1 new decoration on North Ocean
- Added a glowing 'New' icon in Mode Menu when a new Commander or Relic was unlocked

Bugs fixed:
- Objective about discovering underground Mystery Spots gets automatically completed now, if there are no underground Mystery Spots left
- Fixed the bug that allowed to upgrade buildings for an infinite number of times
- Now Order Relic can't be used on a tower that is being upgraded or relocated
- Now towers don't shoot while being under construction, upgraded or relocated
- Now Order Relic 'shooting mode' is closed, if another window is opened
- Now Order Relic can't be used during pause or when the time is stopped
- Embankment and Defensive Dam disappear when the ground below them is destroyed by the boss in the 4th level
- Fixed a minor visual glitch appearing on Embankments
- Now a tooltip for destroying buildings doesn't appear while hovering over Miners Base (which, of course, can't be destroyed)
- Fixed depth value of the Strait that caused some objects in front of it to look like they are behind it
 
Other:
- Added a new visual effects for a few technologies
- Increased collision box of Defensive Dam
- Now chunks of resources drop next to the Shipyard if there is no enough space for resources gained by canceling ship construction
- Now chunks of resources drop from a building if there is no enough space for resources gained by demolishing that building

While these may not be game-changing tweaks, they'll surely add some pleasant variety to what's already been available for a while.

And rest assured, this isn't the end of the road for Flooded. I’ll keep working on it, and there's more to come. Wishing you all a fantastic time and good luck in your battle against the flood!

Enjoy and have fun!
Tymek

notes.title: Post-Release Update #3 - New difficulty level, technologies and some fixes…
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/5f8c3f568df94c585d521f794c6085be40cadb07.png

Hello, folks!

I want to start this post by thanking you all for your feedback since the release of Flooded. Your reports and comments about bugs or missing features have been incredibly helpful in improving the game, so thank you!

I’ve spent the past week working on addressing some of the issues you've mentioned, and I'm happy to announce that there are a ton of improvements in the newest update! Guys, version 1.0.6 is here! 

Just chillin’

One of the biggest new features is the addition of a new difficulty level called "Relaxed". It is now the easiest way to play Flooded - the flood meter fills up slower, which significantly reduces the stress associated with dealing with the flood. I think cozy game fans will love it (and not only them), because it will allow them to focus on building, rather than on surviving. 

What’s more…

In addition to the new difficulty level, I've also added two new technologies - Terraforming and Terraforming II! Both will help in case of water and electricity shortages, but I'll let you discover that yourself! Good luck!

Oh, and are there any component fans here? There is a new one called “Wet Performance Screw” - you should defo try it out! Or maybe you want to test your luck? If so, then check the Mystery Box in the trade menu!

Furthermore, there are plenty of balancing changes, bug fixes, and other small improvements that should make the game even more enjoyable to play. Check out the full changelog below for more details:

New features:

2 new technologies (Terraforming + Terraforming II)
1 new component (Wet Performance Screw)
New difficulty level (Relaxed)
1 new decoration on Rocky Ocean
1 new decoration on Tropical Ocean
You can now cancel ship construction in the queue by clicking it
Added Mystery Box that can be purchased in the trade menu to obtain a random component

Balance changes:

Acid rain doesn't appear in the first era anymore
Now there are more free ground tiles among trees on Tropical Ocean
The island on the 7th level is now bigger
The island on the 9th level is now bigger

Bugs fixed:

Port description changed
Now particles emitted by fire, volcano and explosions don't move while the game is paused or the time is stopped
Now Embankments don't sink during Flood regardless of certain technologies (Melioration II, Artificial Islands II) being developed.
Newly collected components should now arrange on the grid in the right way
Natural Reservoir can't be built multiple times in the same spot anymore
Theo's (Discoverer) passive ability related to finding positive objects in Mystery Spots should now work without issues
Colors of particles emitted when a building is destroyed should now match the building's color
Ice Cream Shop can now be built only once per level (as the building's description claims)
The bug with rivers and fissures not spawning in the 10th level is now less frequent

Other changes:

Buildings that can't be upgraded don't have the level information box in their menu anymore.
Dark Performance Screw icon changed
Now play time statistic at the end of each level does not include time manipulation
Turret's range now increases with its level and is affected by Turret's performance statistic

Thanks again for your support, and don’t forget to leave a review on Steam - it will be very helpful. 

Stay tuned for more!
Tymek

notes.title: Flooded has been out for a week!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/6f5d4b898273ba6ed2f1275fc8e5abbd510f01c9.png

Hello everyone! 👋

Can you believe it's been a whole week since I released Flooded? Time flies! I wanted to use this opportunity to reflect on the past days and share my own impressions on the launch.

Firstly, I'm thrilled with how everything went and I'm over the moon that so many of you played my game. At its peak, 74 people were playing simultaneously, which is an amazing result! What's even better is that, even though it's been several days now, there are still at least a dozen people playing the game almost constantly!

Reviews 🎮

You know what’s exciting? Flooded has been making waves in the gaming world! It's been featured on some of the biggest gaming sites out there, including:

📰 PC Gamer

“I faced some tricky choices as I played: if there's a copper node close to shore, should I set up a mine on it to quickly extract as much as I can? Or should I leave it and build my factory further inland where I know the building won't be swallowed by the ocean within the next few minutes?”

📰 Destructoid

“For being a rather unique premise, Flooded offers a very tight and polished experience. It’s the sort of thing where I’m afraid that if you either add something or take it away, it will stop working. Just a terrific execution of its thesis. I’m not certain it will necessarily soak your socks like some more expansive builders might, but your time spent stranded will be worthwhile.”

📰 Even the Financial Times!

“It’s a compelling combination of base-building, tower defence and real-time strategy whose procedurally generated maps, different modes and £10 price tag more than make up for its relatively short campaign length. And its combination of human and environmental threats is an effective reminder that when it comes to the climate, we are often our own worst enemies.”

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/64a3a03280325090ab937f0e4633368236ae57f8.png

In addition, many well-known creators (like Raptor, Orbital Potato or Lutel) have streamed the game! 

Can you believe it? I still can't!

Thank you! 🙏🏽

Once more, I wanted to send a big thank you to everyone who's been playing Flooded and sharing their thoughts on Steam. Your support means everything to me. I also want to encourage you to leave reviews, as they really help the game reach new people.

Finally, I'm excited to announce that a new update will be released this Friday! It will add some content and fix a couple of the bugs you've been telling me about.

Thanks again for your support, and I can't wait to see you all in the game!
Tymek

notes.title: Tips and tricks 🧰
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/ae913d350ee6335e28eb40aeaf866657a3d87694.png

Hello!

I know Flooded may seem like a simple game (looking at the art style!), but it can sometimes get tricky, especially when you hear the siren and your buildings are about to disappear in the ocean… 
To give you a headstart, I’ve prepared a couple of hints that I hope will help you flow (pun intended) through the levels! 🙂

[olist]
 Remember to build enough Quarters, as they provide you with Miners. To gather resources you need: 


 Open-Pit Mine/Mining Shaft/Underwater Mining Shaft;
 Miners;
 Water.

It’s crucial that you obtain enough Miners to fill all jobs and supply them with the right amount of Water.

 Don’t forget about upgrading buildings from the Action category. A Workshop or Lumber Mill on level 3 can cover even the entire island!

 Think 3 steps ahead - build Embankments, while you still have space. Later on you’ll have to rely on Artificial Ground, which is more expensive.

 Avoid cutting down trees around your Miners’ Base - they can cover your base from enemy fire.

 Learn about your Commander and Relict - not using their perks can make the playthrough more difficult.

 When you think everything is lost, try to uncover Mystery Spots on/under the ground or on the ocean. An epic chest may end up saving your run.

 When leveling and upgrading buildings, start with those farthest from the shore. The ones by the ocean will probably get flooded anyway.

 When you can see that the next flood will take away some buildings, destroy them. This way you’ll at least get back half of the resources used to build them.

 Use shortcut buttons, especially for leveling and destroying buildings. These can be found on the right side of the bottom menu. Once you click on one of them, you will be able to pick which buildings should be upgraded or destroyed. This way you won’t have to click on every single building and upgrade/destroy them from the building’s menu.
[/olist]
Have fun!
Tymek

notes.title: Balance changes and first fixes - post-release update is here!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/6452b28f4bf696a1bcba9d4f391102ba5e9724f2.png

Gamers! 

These past few days have been absolutely crazy! But now the dust has settled and I have the first update for you.

Before I tell you more about the changes, I want to thank all of you for your support, feedback, reviews (especially those on Steam - they mean the world to me) and just for playing Flooded. I am so happy to see that the reception has been positive. It is incredibly helpful in shaping the future of the game.

Update

Now moving on to the update. The most important change involves balancing. Our goal was to make the game challenging. The rising water is supposed to create pressure, so that players need to act fast. However, we can now see that not everyone is enjoying this as much as we do. Because of that I have extended the time for the flood meter to fill and I have reduced the impact of rain on the flood meter (on all difficulty levels). I’m hoping this will make the experience more enjoyable.

I have also added some quality-of-life features: the ability to skip splash screens when launching the game, the possibility to demolish Embankment and Defensive Dam, North Ocean now has 1 new landmark type decoration.

Keep an eye out for further updates and in the meantime, here’s a full changelog:

- Now you can skip splash screens with logos by pressing Space, Enter, Escape or LMB

notes.title: Let's go on a journey!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/90680a5add35602342b66123c84a11a736a100d5.png

Gamers!

Flooded has evolved a lot over the months. It started as a tiny project, developed into the demo that’s still available on Steam, and moved to the form in which it is now. And I have to admit it's not over yet. There is still a long way to go before I get to the place where I wanted to be. 

One of the things I had in mind from the very beginning are biomes.. I knew from the start that I would like to provide you with a variety of levels on which you will be able to face the challenges that Flooded holds. Right now let's focus on the Calm Ocean, the Rocky Ocean, and the Toxic Ocean.

Calm Ocean

The "basic" stage in Flooded is the Calm Ocean. However, it also has some characteristic elements. It’s definitely interesting that here you will be able to see a lot of buildings known from the real world (treat them as easter eggs to capture ;)). 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/d19ffbd5a19ca14fa9a9919be5652191beaff591.png

The island is characterized by a large number of obstacles and relatively many trees. It also features an exclusive mechanic of "Sea Silence", which means that every once in a while the wind may stop blowing, rendering the windmills useless for that period, as they can't produce energy.

Rocky Ocean

You will definitely not run out of mobile service here, and Wi-Fi should also work well. This is due to the numerous radio and cellular network antennas that surround Rocky Island. You never know when you’ll want to play Candy Crush during a break from saving the world, so it’s cool…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/b72c43472476a644899e9784b7aeedcf071ba347.png

There are no trees on the island, but you can notice various ores and a lot of stones. Moreover, occasional earthquakes can occur - they won’t only damage buildings, but can also create cracks in the ground. Dangerous and somehow exciting!

Toxic Ocean

I have recently mentioned the Toxic Ocean on my social media (links below - feel free to follow). Here you can definitely find more trees than stones and many industrial buildings around the island.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/972bf7959c7839bf020cc633f1eceeab45540a62.png

As if that was not enough, you can spot oil stains around the island. Be aware of them, because they will impair the productivity of filters. Still not scared? Sometimes you can encounter acid rain that damages trees, buildings, and units. It's not easy to work in such conditions!

First things first…

As I mentioned, this is just a chunk of what awaits you in the full version of Flooded. However, you can already see that depending on the biome, you’ll have to take a different approach. It may turn out that what gives juicy fruits in one place, will be a path to quick failure in another.

A good hero will always adapt, though, so good luck!

See ya!

notes.title: Progress abhors a vacuum
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/44122eac7b444626138387925cfe8f701a4bc09e.png

What’s up?

Recently, I’ve been quite busy, which is related to the upcoming PAX West 2022 in Seattle. As I said a few weeks ago, I’ll be there with Flooded (more information and booth number HERE). Yet - sometimes you have to slow down and remind yourself that even small steps bring us closer to our goal. It’s called progress. 

The simplest facilitators of it are: clear rules, a vision of the finish line, and a reward system. All three are in Flooded. How? Inspired by strategy games with which I fell in love as a kid - by adding the eras system.

Up the ladder...

In Flooded, the gameplay can be divided into four stages - the Era of Mining (highlighting the extraction of ores and search for new deposits), the Era of Electricity (adding electricity production), the Era of Expansion (focusing on placing the buildings that can be placed on the ocean), and the New Era (allowing to complete remaining tasks).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/47a64dea9017e6163a9d131fa18789a80c7fc6e9.png

Each of them increases the number of possibilities that we have and provides tasks to structure the level and help the player. For example - entering the Era of Electricity allows us to construct buildings related to... Yes, you guessed - electricity. 

Closer to the end

As I mentioned, the main factor behind this shape of the game is the desire to engage the player. We all love when our efforts are rewarded (just remember the satisfaction of a D- at school)! What’s more, many games introduce intermediate points in larger missions - no one wants to keep players without gratification for too long, as it may negatively affect their enthusiasm.

Luckily, the genre and form of Flooded make it possible to weave such a system in a very natural way. While playing, we feel that we have a tangible influence on how the world is created, a world that seems to be heading towards a wet end.

Thanks for coming and see you soon!

notes.title: Meet the Team…
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/8b68bbd6529f1a2bf4a76f30315d5cdb7157b5a3.png

Before you set off, you should assemble a team… And its most important component will always be the commander, who is in charge of coordinating the team’s actions, uniting the group and deciding on the most important things.

In Flooded, before each game, you will be able to choose a commander to manage your attempts to survive a historical flood. However, they will not be the same - each of them offers specific perks and special ways to reach your goals. Today I will introduce you to some of them!

Myles (Specialization: Strategy)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/92b31bdf64c26b784b52694c6bdfce3dbeb15e48.png

Bonus: Adjacent buildings of the same type work more efficiently.

The first character is a slim man with dark hair combed in an old-fashioned way. He is great at building various strategies and his main strength is paperwork. He makes up for his physical shortcomings with his cleverness and analytical approach to each problem.

Ellen (Specialization: Construction)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/07554fdf71703a2adab7e9f83729a214e2ae5ae9.png

Bonus: Buildings can be relocated.

A hardworking woman with a ponytail always hidden under a helmet. You must know she is the only one who has never worked in a mine. However, Ellen is not afraid to get her hands dirty, and her experience in other industries is a big advantage in a natural crisis.

Henry (Specialization: Defense)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/6fa0ef25f9684a3b3d53510bcf46807940f8c72f.png

Bonus: The default durability of buildings is increased.

This guy is the opposite of Myles - a characterful and well-built blonde who believes in muscle strength. Although, it must be noted, he never uses it to hurt another person. Henry is mild-mannered by nature, but very charismatic. He can easily lead a group of miners and motivate them to work harder! 

Thomas (Specialization: Technologies)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/6ada42a0e01cebecbc1d35c3e63dce73a5b1d17d.png

Bonus: Buildings have an additional level of development.

The youngest of the group of potential commanders and probably the most distracted. However, it is a textbook image of a real genius. His short-lived enthusiasm does not allow him to finish the tasks he has already started, but his impressive knowledge can help you escape the island… The choice is yours!

See ya!

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/1fc865ca1ef7b634a21ac780bab09ebb013d3eec.png

Everything has a beginning and every effect has a cause. The linearity of life, the principle of interaction and all that blah, blah, blah. Sounds philosophical? Maybe, but that’s the reality. And in the case of Flooded - in retrospect - I was not expecting what the future was about to bring me.

How did it all start?

I love creating games, and one of the best options for making one from A to Z are all kinds of game jams. This is a good opportunity to test your skills and knowledge of tools, as well as meet many people from the industry.

However, in order to discover new horizons, I assumed that I would try something different for every event of this type - after all, the market is flooded with game genres. The idea for what you know today as “Flooded” was born during Miedź Jam 2021. The theme of the game jam was “The Future is Copper” (“miedz” means “copper” in Polish).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42149552/00061b1e9cb162bb9566c65f5610d0387d1d0388.png

I have never done isometric strategies before, and let's agree, the subject of the event itself asked for something like that. This is how I came up with a plan for "Copper Island" - an RTS game about escaping an island, using mined resources. 

Well, there was just one important thing - I was lacking an element in this idea that would really distinguish it from other strategy games…

And then I thought "hmm, what if I made this island shrink?..." The rest was easy, as I built all the other mechanics around this concept. A week of work, turning the vision into reality and continuous programming that resulted in getting a third place at the game jam!

[previewyoutube=K3BU_IzD5dY;full][/previewyoutube]

Sail on the wave!

The project received really positive feedback and a lot of voices encouraged me to further develop what I have managed to create during these seven days. And although I did not intend to wade into it at first (I am not used to staying with jam games - surprisingly, without time pressure, the work is harder), sometimes when life gives you lemons, you might want to try making the most delicious lemonade.

This is the exact decision that I made in the case of this project. “Copper Island” was renamed to “Flooded”, and similar thing happened to my life plans - they completely changed. Nevertheless, this is just the beginning of the story, as it turned out there were a lot of surprises waiting for me on the way… But I’ll tell you more about it some other time. 

Stay tuned!
